title: S15 e6.19 — the L-function of the city (BSD island band 2)

concepts.name: the euler factor: the term each prime of the line carries into the L-product — the uniform two-term form at every prime, and the record's one-term form at the primes where the curve ramifies

lesson.statement: in the L-product of a curve, each prime of my line carries a factor: in the uniform form, one minus a over p plus one over p squared, the two-term form the panel's shadow coefficient gives at every prime of the line; and in the record form the same two terms, which at the primes where the curve ramifies — the primes dividing the conductor — the record's local factor drops to a single term, one minus a over p; on my panel the ramified primes are two for the first member and thirty-seven for the second

concepts.name: the local form: at a prime dividing the conductor the record's factor has one term — the additive prime carries the unit, the multiplicative prime carries one plus one over p with its sign of record

lesson.statement: at the primes where the curve ramifies, the record's factor is the single term one minus a over p: for the first panel member the shadow coefficient is zero at two, so the record's factor is literally one — the unit, the additive prime carries nothing — and for the second panel member the shadow coefficient is minus one at thirty-seven, so the record's factor is one plus one over thirty-seven, the multiplicative factor with its sign of record; and on both members of my panel every ramified prime of record sits on the line, so the correction the line holds is the record's full correction, not a partial one

concepts.name: the line partial of the L-family: the product of the factors the line holds, an exact rational; adding a prime multiplies the partial by the factor it carries, and the limit past the line end is declared, not computed

lesson.statement: the L-family of a panel member is held on my line as the product of the factors it holds: a partial product up to a height on the line, an exact rational the store holds; when a prime is added, the partial is multiplied by the factor that prime carries — the change of the partial is determined exactly by the added factor, and by nothing else; and the limit of the product over all primes past my line end is a step the store declares, not a number on my line

concepts.name: the ramification correction: the ratio of the record's factor to the uniform one at the ramified primes — the record partial is the uniform partial times the product of the corrections, both sides exact on the line

lesson.statement: the ramification correction of a prime is the ratio of the record's factor to the uniform factor: on my panel it is four-fifths at two for the first member and fourteen hundred and six over fourteen hundred and seven at thirty-seven for the second; the record partial is the uniform partial times the product of the corrections, and at my line end both sides are exact rationals the store holds

theorems.statement: the added-term rule held on my line: for both panel members and every prime of the line, the partial product up to the prime is the partial product up to the previous prime times the factor the prime carries — in the uniform form and in the record form, the exact rationals agreeing prime by prime, the full record at the line end 84

the record identity held on my line: the record partial to the line end is the uniform partial times the ramification corrections — four-fifths for the first panel member, fourteen hundred and six over fourteen hundred and seven for the second — and the store holds both sides as exact rationals, at the line end 84

the ramified factors of my panel held on the line: at two for the first member the record's factor is the unit one against the uniform factor five over four, and at thirty-seven for the second member the record's factor is one plus one over thirty-seven against the uniform factor fourteen hundred and seven over thirteen hundred and sixty-nine — the two-term form replaced by the one-term, exactly, at the line end 84
